title: The origin of jinn, moral responsibility, and the qarin
claim: Presents the origin of jinn from fire, debates over their progenitor, their moral agency and free will, and the nature of the qarin.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: السلام عليكم في هذه الحلقة نتابع الحديث عن أهم الأسئلة الجوهرية المتعلقة بعالم الجن نتحدث عن أصلهم من هو أبوهم لماذا خلقوا
mentions.excerpt_note: Opening lines of the episode.

notes: Complete normalized Arabic transcript inspected. Video sets the thematic outline and sequence of topics.

title: Hadith on seeking knowledge for display or contention
locator: Jami al-Tirmidhi 2654 (Kitab al-Ilm); Sunan Ibn Majah 253, 254
claim: Whoever seeks knowledge to compete with scholars, argue with the foolish, or attract people s attention, Allah will admit him to Hell.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: من تعلم العلم ليباهي به العلماء أو يماري به السفهاء أو يصرف وجوه الناس إليه أدخله الله جهنم
mentions.excerpt_note: Spoken by the presenter emphasizing sincere intentions in investigating the unseen.

notes: Narrated from Ka b ibn Malik and Hudhayfah. Graded Hasan by al-Tirmidhi and Sahih lighayrihi by al-Albani.

title: Quran 55:15
claim: And He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: المتفق عليه أصلهم أنهم خلقوا من مارج من نار، كما جاء في الآية الكريمة.
mentions.excerpt_note: Cited in discussion of the primordial substance from which jinn were created.

notes: Primary Quranic text verified. Al-Rahman 55:15.

title: Sahih Muslim 2996: Creation of angels, jinn, and Adam
locator: Sahih Muslim 2996 (Kitab al-Zuhd wa al-Raqa iq, hadith 60)
claim: Angels were created from light, jinn from a smokeless flame of fire, and Adam from that which has been described to you.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: خلقت الملائكة من نور، وخلق الجان من مارج من نار، وخلق آدم مما وصف لكم
mentions.excerpt_note: Report of A ishah directly quoted.

notes: Sahih Muslim 2996 verified. Foundational textual evidence for the distinct elemental origins of angels, jinn, and humans.

title: Hawatif al-Jinan by Ibn Abi al-Dunya
locator: Hawatif al-Jinan, narratives on voices and funerals of jinn
claim: Compilation of historical anecdotes describing voices and funerals of jinn heard by humans.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: كتاب الهواتف لابن أبي الدنيا الذي جمع كثيرًا من الروايات منها مثلًا أنهم كانوا يسمعون الجن يشيعون موتاهم ليذهبوا إلى دفنهم
mentions.excerpt_note: Cited regarding the dispute over whether jinn corpses are buried or vanish.

notes: Verified work by Ibn Abi al-Dunya (d. 281 AH). Presenter notes these are anecdotal transmissions that do not establish normative fiqh or theological certainty.

title: Quran 18:50
claim: Iblis was of the jinn and he rebelled against the command of his Lord; will you then take him and his progeny as allies besides Me?

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: الدليل افتتخذونه وذريته أولياء من دوني... كان من الجن ففسق عن أمر ربه
mentions.excerpt_note: Central verse in discussing the lineage of jinn and Iblis.

notes: Quran 18:50 text and classical commentary verified.

title: Scholarly debate on whether Iblis is the progenitor of all jinn
locator: Majmu al-Fatawa 4/235; Tafsir al-Tabari 18:50; Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:50
claim: Widely held classical opinion that Iblis is the father of all jinn, analogous to Adam for humanity.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: الرأي الأكثر انتشارًا بين علمائنا أن الجن أولاد إبليس وهو مثل آدم. نقل هذا عن ابن عباس والحسن البصري ومجاهد وقتادة واختاره شيخ الإسلام
mentions.excerpt_note: Presenter cites this major classical position before presenting counterarguments and alternatives.

notes: Documented in classical tafsir and fatwa literature. The presenter argues for an alternative view that Iblis was an individual from a pre-existing species.

title: Traditions concerning the Hinn and Binn
claim: Folklore concerning pre-Adamic creatures who allegedly inhabited earth before being expelled by jinn.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: فقال بعض علماء التفسير خلقت الجن قبل آدم عليه السلام وكان قبلهم في الأرض الحن والبن فسلط الله الجن عليهم فقاتلوهم
mentions.excerpt_note: Presenter explicitly notes these stories lack authentic chain of transmission.

notes: Recorded in classical chronicles and tafsir works as unauthenticated historical reports (Isra iliyyat).

title: Narration of al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas on the progeny of Iblis
locator: Tafsir al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan), Surah al-Kahf 18:50, narration #23772
claim: Report stating that devils are the children of Iblis who do not die except with Iblis.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: وقد روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال الشياطين ولدان إبليس لا يموتون إلا مع إبليس
mentions.excerpt_note: Cited to examine competing narrations attributed to early authorities.

notes: Tafsir al-Tabari 18:50 records this via al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas. The transmission chain has well-known breaks (inqita ).

title: Traditions naming Sumya or al-Jann as the forefather of jinn
claim: Early narrations identifying the ancestor of jinn as an entity named Sumya or al-Jann rather than Iblis.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: الرأي الثاني وحتى روي أيضاً عن ابن عباس أن أبو الجن ليس إبليس بل شخص آخر اسمه سوما أو سوميا
mentions.excerpt_note: Discussed as a secondary opinion found in early commentaries.

notes: Recorded in early tafsir literature (al-Tabari, al-Baghawi, Ibn Kathir). Largely based on transmissions from Ibn Abbas influenced by pre-Islamic/Israelite narratives.

title: Hadith on the three classes of jinn
locator: Al-Mustadrak ala al-Sahihayn 2/456 (#3702); al-Mu jam al-Kabir 22/214; Sahih al-Jami 3114
claim: Jinn are of three classes: one with wings flying in the air, one of serpents and dogs, and one that alights and travels.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: الجن ثلاثة أصناف صنف لهم أجنحة يطيرون في الهواء وصنف حيات وكلاب وصنف يحلون ويظعنون
mentions.excerpt_note: Authentic prophetic description of diversity among jinn.

notes: Narrated from Abu Tha labah al-Khushani. Graded Sahih by al-Hakim, al-Dhahabi, and al-Albani (Sahih al-Jami 3114).

title: Quran 51:56
claim: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: الغاية الأساسية من خلقهم هي العبادة وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون
mentions.excerpt_note: Primary proof of moral accountability and free will in jinn.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: يبحث فيها الا بمصادر الوحيده وهذا فصلناه في حلقه سابقه ارجو العوده اليها وقلنا انه يمكن ان تكون هناك مصادر معرفه ماخوذه حتى من غير المؤمنين ونكرر ايضا ان الجن
mentions.excerpt_note: Exact normalized ASR anchor, first up to four segments of the stated discussion range; not corrected Arabic or a quotation from the independent source.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: مع كل ما سبق الجنسان متساويان في التكليف ولو قلنا ايضا انه بعض الحيوانات ربما تكون مفضله على الانس في بعض المزايا كما قلنا عن الجن مثلا فلدينا مثلا قدرات عند
mentions.excerpt_note: Exact normalized ASR anchor, first up to four segments of the stated discussion range; not corrected Arabic or a quotation from the independent source.

notes: Quran 51:56 verified. The definitive theological basis for taklif across humans and jinn.

title: Quran 72:11–14
claim: And among us are the righteous, and among us are others; we were of divided ways... and among us are Muslims and among us are the unjust.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: وأن منا الصالحون ومنا دون ذلك كنا طرائق قددا... وأن منا المسلمون ومنا القاسطون
mentions.excerpt_note: Direct testimony of the believing jinn recorded in revelation.

notes: Surah al-Jinn 72:11, 14 verified.

title: Ibn al-Qayyim on the moral tiers of jinn
locator: Tariq al-Hijratayn wa Bab al-Sa adatayn, pp. 382–383
claim: Ibn al-Qayyim states that jinn are divided into three ranks just like humans: righteous, intermediate, and disbelievers.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: فلذلك قال ابن القيم: هم ثلاث درجات مثل الإنس صالحين ودون الصالحين وكفار
mentions.excerpt_note: Paraphrased from Tariq al-Hijratayn.

notes: Primary locator verified in Tariq al-Hijratayn. Corroborates the parity of accountability between humans and jinn.

title: Ta rif Amm bi Din al-Islam by Ali al-Tantawi
locator: Ta rif Amm bi Din al-Islam, section on the unseen and angels/jinn, pp. 35–37
claim: Sheikh Ali al-Tantawi s introductory book suggesting devils may have been created without choice, which the presenter critiques as anomalous.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: هذا الرأي الشاذ نجده في كتاب مثلاً عند الشيخ علي الطنطاوي رحمه الله, كتاب اسمه تعريف عام بدين الإسلام
mentions.excerpt_note: Critiqued for conflicting with Quran 51:56.

notes: Verified locator in Tantawi s work. The presenter respectfully identifies this point as an isolated error derived from non-Islamic theological concepts.

title: Little Nicky (2000 film)
claim: Hollywood fantasy film portraying the devil and his progeny as rulers of the underworld interacting with humanity.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: في فيلم اسمه ليتل نيكي, فيلم صدر في هوليود في عام 2000, من بطولة آدم ساندلر... الشيطان يدخل في صراع مع أولاده
mentions.excerpt_note: Cultural example of Western conception of devils as rulers of hell rather than prisoners in torment.

notes: Film details and plot summary verified. Used to illustrate cultural misconceptions.

title: Hellboy (character and film)
claim: Western fantasy depiction of a demon who fights on the side of good.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: في شخصية أخرى مشهورة اسمها هيل بوي
mentions.excerpt_note: Contrasting Western fallen angel lore with Islamic theology of voluntary moral agency.

notes: Cultural reference verified.

title: Weak report claiming a third of jinn were created as devils subject to punishment
locator: Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Da ifah wa al-Mawdu ah #2921
claim: Report claiming that one-third of jinn were created as devils upon whom punishment is inevitable.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: فلذلك هذا الحديث صنفه الألباني في سلسلة الأحاديث الضعيفة والموضوعة. ويتعارض مع الحديث الصحيح
mentions.excerpt_note: Presenter cites al-Albani s grading to demonstrate that devils were not predestined to evil without choice.

notes: Al-Albani designates this narration as Da if jiddan (very weak) in al-Da ifah #2921, noting it conflicts with authenticated reports and the Qur an.

title: Quran 38:84–85
claim: I will surely fill Hell with you and with those among them that follow you all together.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: قال فالحق والحق أقول لأملأن جهنم منك وممن تبعك منهم أجمعين
mentions.excerpt_note: Proof that Iblis and his followers will be punished in the Fire.

notes: Surah Sad 38:84–85 verified.

title: Quran 14:22
claim: Satan will say when the matter has been concluded: Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth... I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: وقال الشيطان لما قضي الأمر إن الله وعدكم وعد الحق ووعدتكم فأخلفتكم وما كان لي عليكم من سلطان
mentions.excerpt_note: Decisive proof that Iblis possesses no coercive power and is himself tormented.

notes: Surah Ibrahim 14:22 verified.

title: Quran 6:112
claim: And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy—devils from mankind and jinn.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: وكذلك جعلنا لكل نبي عدوًا شياطين الإنس والجن. فالشيطان وصف وهو لقب
mentions.excerpt_note: Linguistic and theological explanation that shaytan is a functional descriptor of rebel transgressors.

notes: Surah al-An am 6:112 verified.

title: Iblis by Abbas Mahmud al-Aqqad
locator: Iblis, Dar al-Ma arif, introductory linguistic studies
claim: Al-Aqqad argues that Iblis is an ancient proper name found across multiple languages, rather than merely an Arabic derivation from ablasa.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: العقاد في كتابه إبليس قال إنه وجد كلمة إبليس موجودة في كل أو في الكثير من اللغات والأديان السابقة
mentions.excerpt_note: Presenter cites al-Aqqad in rejecting far-fetched Arabic etymologies for the proper noun Iblis.

notes: Verified monograph by Egyptian literary scholar Abbas Mahmud al-Aqqad (published 1958).

title: Quran 50:23, 27
claim: And his companion will say: This is what is with me ready... His companion will say: Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, but he was in extreme error.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: وقال قرينه هذا ما لدي عتيد. قال قرينه ربنا ما أطغيته ولكن كان في ضلال بعيد
mentions.excerpt_note: Scriptural foundation for the qarin.

notes: Surah Qaf 50:23, 27 verified.

title: Quran 43:36
claim: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful—We appoint for him a devil, so he becomes for him an intimate companion.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: ومن يعش عن ذكر الرحمن نقيض له شيطانًا فهو له قرين
mentions.excerpt_note: Shows appointment of a devil companion as consequence of spiritual heedlessness.

notes: Surah al-Zukhruf 43:36 verified.

title: Sahih Muslim 2814a: The appointment of the qarin
claim: There is none among you but has been assigned his companion from among the jinn. They said: And you, O Messenger of Allah? He said: And me, but Allah helped me against him so he submitted (or: I am safe from him), and he commands me only to do good.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: ما منكم من أحد إلا وقد وكل به قرينه من الجن. قالوا وإياك يا رسول الله قال وإياي
mentions.excerpt_note: Report of Ibn Mas ud directly cited.

notes: Sahih Muslim 2814a verified. Demonstrates that the assignment of a companion does not compel a person nor does it mean the companion was created without choice.

title: Sahih Muslim 2815: A ishah s question regarding the shaytan companion
claim: A ishah reports that when the Prophet asked if her shaytan had come to her, she inquired whether every person has a shaytan, and he confirmed it.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: حديث عائشة لما غارت عليه قال أقد جاءك شيطانك قالت يا رسول الله أو معي شيطان؟ قال نعم. قالت ومع كل إنسان؟ قال نعم.
mentions.excerpt_note: Corroborates the universality of the trial.

notes: Sahih Muslim 2815 verified.

title: Quran 4:90
claim: And if Allah had willed, He could have given them power over you, and they would have fought you.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: ولو شاء الله لسلطهم عليكم فلقاتلوكم
mentions.excerpt_note: Explaining that divine enablement of adversaries is a testing framework, not an endorsement of evil.

notes: Surah al-Nisa 4:90 verified.

title: Quran 47:4
claim: And if Allah had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them, but [He intended] to test some of you by means of others.

mentions.raw_excerpt_ar: ولو يشاء الله لانتصر منهم ولكن ليبلو بعضكم ببعض
mentions.excerpt_note: Divine wisdom behind allowing devils and opponents to test believers.

notes: Surah Muhammad 47:4 verified.
